## Prepare PHYSEQ objects

We combine DESIGN, TAXA and COUNT tables to a PHYSEQ object. the we define:\
- **low abundant phyla:** mean of the phyla abundance in all samples \<= 0.1%\
- **high abundant phyla:** mean of the phyla abundance in all samples \> 0.1%

```{r}
#| label: get melted PHYSEQs
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

# Data as PHYLOSEQ object
get_PHYSEQ_objects <- function(design, data, taxa, microbial_load=F){

  #change order for melting later and (remove species for fungi and oomycetes)
  taxa <- taxa[,c("labels", "kingdom", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus", "ASV_ID")]
  
  #create phyloseq::phyloseq objects
  design <- as.data.frame(design)
  rownames(design) <- design$bc_ID
  data <- as.matrix(data)
  taxa <- as.matrix(taxa[rownames(data),])
  physeq <- phyloseq::phyloseq(sample_data(design),
                     otu_table(data, taxa_are_rows=T),
                     tax_table(taxa))
  
  # agglomerate data by labels 
  physeq_phyla <- phyloseq::taxglom(physeq, "labels") # merge by 'labels' 
  
  #copy for microbial load because we can't norm them
  if(microbial_load){
    #use this at the end, other is only to get high and low abu
    physeq_phyla_unnorm <- physeq_phyla
    # melt phyloseq::phyloseq object
    physeq_phyla_melt_unnorm <- phyloseq::psmelt(physeq_phyla) 
    # Defining ASV colors by labels
    physeq_phyla_melt_unnorm$labels <- as.factor(physeq_phyla_melt_unnorm$labels)
    physeq_phyla_melt_unnorm$cols <- as.character(physeq_phyla_melt_unnorm$labels)
  }
  
  #norm
  physeq_phyla <- phyloseq::transform_sample_counts(physeq_phyla, function(x) 100 * x/sum(x)) 
  # melt phyloseq::phyloseq object
  physeq_phyla_melt <- phyloseq::psmelt(physeq_phyla) 
  # Defining ASV colors by labels
  physeq_phyla_melt$labels <- as.factor(physeq_phyla_melt$labels)
  physeq_phyla_melt$cols <- as.character(physeq_phyla_melt$labels)

  #threshold
  threshold <- ifelse(microbial_load, 1, 0.1) #higher threshold when there is no host DNA
  
  # Defining high abundant phyla
  # phyla with MEAN abundances higher than 1% relative abundances
  physeq_phyla_abu <-  rownames(otu_table(physeq_phyla))[apply(otu_table(physeq_phyla), 1, mean, na.rm=T) > threshold] #set it to 0.1 instead of 1 because we have a lot of plant seqs
  try(physeq_phyla_abuP <- tax_table(physeq_phyla)[rownames(tax_table(physeq_phyla)) %in% physeq_phyla_abu, "labels"], silent=T)
  
  # Defining low abundant phyla
  # phyla with MEAN abundances lower than 1% relative abundances
  physeq_phyla_low <-  rownames(otu_table(physeq_phyla))[apply(otu_table(physeq_phyla), 1, mean, na.rm=T) <= threshold]
  try(physeq_phyla_lowP <- tax_table(physeq_phyla)[rownames(tax_table(physeq_phyla)) %in% physeq_phyla_low, "labels"], silent=T)

  # subsetting the color vector to abundant labels and classes
  # delete labels name of low-abundant phyla (for plot) and put them at the bottom
  physeq_phyla_melt$labels_2 <- as.character(physeq_phyla_melt$labels)
  try(physeq_phyla_melt[physeq_phyla_melt$labels_2 %in% physeq_phyla_lowP, ]$labels_2 <- "Low abundant phyla", silent = T)
  physeq_phyla_melt$labels_2 <- as.factor(physeq_phyla_melt$labels_2)
  
  #use unnorm data for microbial load
  if(microbial_load){
    physeq_phyla <- physeq_phyla_unnorm #overwrite
    physeq_phyla_melt_unnorm$labels_2 <- physeq_phyla_melt$labels_2 #add low and high abu and overwrite
    physeq_phyla_melt <- physeq_phyla_melt_unnorm
  }
  
  #return(list(physeq, physeq_phyla_melt, bcol_class))
  return(list(physeq, physeq_phyla_melt))

}

#get PHYSEQ
temp <- get_PHYSEQ_objects(bDESIGN, bCOUNTm_norm, bTAXA_norm)
bPHYSEQ <- temp[[1]]
bPHYSEQ_phyla_melt <- temp[[2]]

temp <- get_PHYSEQ_objects(fDESIGN, fCOUNTm_norm, fTAXA_norm)
fPHYSEQ <- temp[[1]]
fPHYSEQ_phyla_melt <- temp[[2]]

temp <- get_PHYSEQ_objects(oDESIGN, oCOUNTm_norm, oTAXA_norm)
oPHYSEQ <- temp[[1]]
oPHYSEQ_phyla_melt <- temp[[2]]

rm(temp)

```

In a last step, we add samples removed in *01_Import_Normalization.qmd* as dummy variables with 0 reads which allows to create nicely aligned plots in the next step.

```{r}
#| label: add removed samples
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

# Ensure all samples appear in plot data even if they had zero reads
# For plotting purposes: adds dummy rows for samples missing in PHYSEQ_melt
# by copying one metadata row from PHYSEQ_melt_all and setting abundance to 0.

#function to add missing samples with abu 0
add_missing_samples <- function(PHYSEQ_melt, PHYSEQ_melt_all){
  
  #get all samples
  all_samples <- unique(PHYSEQ_melt_all$sample_nr)

  for(s in all_samples){
    #test if missing
    if(!(s %in% PHYSEQ_melt$sample_nr)){
      #df to add
      to_add <- PHYSEQ_melt_all[PHYSEQ_melt_all$sample_nr==s,,drop=F] #get data to add from other datasets
      to_add <- to_add[1,,drop=F] #select only first entry
      to_add$Abundance <- 0 #change abu to 0
      to_add$labels_2 <- "Low abundant phyla"
      #add
      PHYSEQ_melt <- rbind(PHYSEQ_melt, to_add)
    }
  }
  #return
  return(PHYSEQ_melt)
}

#concat all
PHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_combined <- rbind(bPHYSEQ_phyla_melt, fPHYSEQ_phyla_melt, oPHYSEQ_phyla_melt)

#add missing samples (for plot)
bPHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_combined <- add_missing_samples(bPHYSEQ_phyla_melt, PHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_combined)
fPHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_combined <- add_missing_samples(fPHYSEQ_phyla_melt, PHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_combined)
oPHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_combined <- add_missing_samples(oPHYSEQ_phyla_melt, PHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_combined)

```

## Relative abundances

We show the relative microbial abundance of each phlya and the host. The host DNA was 25x diluted. The scaled plot shows the data with diluted host DNA while we multiplied the host abundance 25 times to get original host abundance showed in the unscaled plot.

```{r}
#| label: function abundance fig
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

#plot_abundance() generates a faceted barplot of microbial relative abundances or microbial load values (depending on microbial_load = TRUE/FALSE) from a melted psmelt()-style data.frame.

plot_abundance <- function(PHYSEQ_melt, title, microbial_load=F){

  #create df for the plot
  df <- PHYSEQ_melt
  df <- aggregate(df$Abundance, by=list(df$Sample, df$condition, df$line, df$labels_2, df$sample_nr), function(x) mean(x, na.rm=T))
  colnames(df) <- c("sample", "condition", "line", "labels_2", "sample_nr", "Abundance")
  
  if(!(microbial_load)){
      #normalise abu to 100% per sample
      for(id in unique(df$sample)){df$Abundance[df$sample==id] <- (df$Abundance[df$sample==id] / sum(df$Abundance[df$sample==id])) *100}
  }
  
  #define color matrix
  names <- (PHYSEQ_melt$labels_2) %>% unique()
  getPalette <-  colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(11, "Spectral"))#function to increase palette
  col_taxa <- getPalette(length(names))
  abu <- aggregate(PHYSEQ_melt$Abundance, list(PHYSEQ_melt$labels_2), sum)
  abu <- abu[order(abu$x, decreasing = F),]
  abu <- abu[c(which(abu$Group.1!="Low abundant phyla"), which(abu$Group.1=="Low abundant phyla")),] #set low abu phyla to end
  #abu <- abu[c(which(abu$Group.1!="unassigned"), which(abu$Group.1=="unassigned")),] #set unassigned phyla to end
  abu <- abu[c(which(abu$Group.1!="Host"), which(abu$Group.1=="Host")),] #set host to end
  names(col_taxa) <- abu$Group.1
  
  #adapt colors
  col_taxa[names(col_taxa) == "Host"] <- "palegreen4"
  col_taxa[names(col_taxa) == "unassigned"] <- "grey90"
  col_taxa[names(col_taxa) == "Low abundant phyla"] <- "grey50"
  
  #factors
  df$labels_2 <- factor(df$labels_2, levels=names(col_taxa)[names(col_taxa) %in% df$labels_2])
  
  #ylab and ylim for lines
  ylab <- ifelse(!(microbial_load), "Relative abundance [%]", "Relative abundance [Microbial seqs / Host seq]")
  ylim <- aggregate(df$Abundance, list(df$sample_nr), function(x) sum(x, na.rm=T))[,2] %>% max()

  #plot
  fig <- ggplot(df, aes_string(x="sample_nr", y="Abundance", fill="labels_2")) +
    geom_bar(stat="identity")+
    xlab("") +
    ylab(ylab) +
    scale_colour_manual(values=col_taxa)+
    scale_fill_manual(values=col_taxa) +
    #guides(fill=guide_legend(title="Phylum"))+
    ggh4x::facet_nested( ~ line + condition, scale="free_x", space="free_x", nest_line = element_line())+
    geom_segment(x=-Inf,xend=Inf,y=(ylim*1.05),yend=(ylim*1.05), lwd=1)+ #add lines under WT / bx1
    geom_segment(x=-Inf,xend=Inf,y=ylim,yend=ylim,lwd=0.2, col="black")+ #box around grids
    geom_segment(x=-Inf,xend=Inf,y=0,yend=0,lwd=0.2, col="black")+ #box around grids
    ggtitle(title)+
    theme_minimal()+
    #theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))
    theme(axis.text.x=element_blank(), axis.ticks.x=element_blank(), panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())


  return(list(col_taxa, fig))
}

```

## Taxonomy plot with unscaled relative abundances

```{r}
#| label: unscale data
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

#To rescale host ASV abundances in the count matrix COUNT based on a known dilution factor (e.g. 25×). This allows host and microbial sequences to be compared on their original proportions, which is critical when estimating microbial load.
#function to unscale

unscale_COUNT <- function(COUNT, TAXA, scaling_factor){
  #unscale
  hostOTUs <- rownames(TAXA)[TAXA$labels=="Host"]
  COUNT[rownames(COUNT) %in% hostOTUs,] <- COUNT[rownames(COUNT) %in% hostOTUs,] * scaling_factor
  #normalise to 100% per sample
  #COUNT <- (COUNT/colSums(COUNT))*100
  return(COUNT)
}

#unscale
bCOUNTm_unscaled <- unscale_COUNT(bCOUNTm_norm, bTAXA_norm, 25)
fCOUNTm_unscaled <- unscale_COUNT(fCOUNTm_norm, fTAXA_norm, 25)

#get PHYSEQ
```

## Microbial load

In a next step we calculate the microbial load (microbial sequences / host sequences) for each sample.

### Taxonomy plot with microbial loads

```{r}
#| label: microbial load data
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

#function to compute microbial load
microbial_load_COUNT <- function(COUNT, TAXA){
  hostOTUs <- rownames(TAXA)[TAXA$labels=="Host"]
  #get microbial load per sample
  for(id in colnames(COUNT)){
    
    #calculate microbial load
    host_abu <- sum(COUNT[rownames(COUNT)%in%hostOTUs, colnames(COUNT)==id])
    COUNT[!(rownames(COUNT)%in%hostOTUs), colnames(COUNT)==id] <- COUNT[!(rownames(COUNT)%in%hostOTUs), colnames(COUNT)==id] / host_abu
  }
  #remove host (no longer needed)
  COUNT <- COUNT[!(rownames(COUNT)%in%hostOTUs),]
  return(COUNT)
}

#microbial load
bCOUNTm_unscaled_ml <- microbial_load_COUNT(bCOUNTm_unscaled, bTAXA_norm)
fCOUNTm_unscaled_ml <- microbial_load_COUNT(fCOUNTm_unscaled, fTAXA_norm)
oCOUNTm_unscaled_ml <- microbial_load_COUNT(oCOUNTm_unscaled, oTAXA_norm)

#TAXA without host
bTAXA_norm_ml <- bTAXA_norm[bTAXA_norm$labels!="Host",]
fTAXA_norm_ml <- fTAXA_norm[fTAXA_norm$labels!="Host",]
oTAXA_norm_ml <- oTAXA_norm[oTAXA_norm$labels!="Host",]


#get PHYSEQ
temp <- get_PHYSEQ_objects(bDESIGN, bCOUNTm_unscaled_ml, bTAXA_norm_ml, microbial_load = T)
bPHYSEQ_unscaled_ml <- temp[[1]]
bPHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_ml <- temp[[2]]

temp <- get_PHYSEQ_objects(fDESIGN, fCOUNTm_unscaled_ml, fTAXA_norm_ml, microbial_load = T)
fPHYSEQ_unscaled_ml <- temp[[1]]
fPHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_ml <- temp[[2]]

temp <- get_PHYSEQ_objects(oDESIGN, oCOUNTm_unscaled_ml, oTAXA_norm_ml, microbial_load = T)
oPHYSEQ_unscaled_ml <- temp[[1]]
oPHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_ml <- temp[[2]]

rm(temp)

#add missing samples (for plot)
bPHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_ml_all <- add_missing_samples(bPHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_ml, PHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_combined)
fPHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_ml_all <- add_missing_samples(fPHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_ml, PHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_combined)
oPHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_ml_all <- add_missing_samples(oPHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_ml, PHYSEQ_phyla_melt_unscaled_combined)
```

### Differences in microbial load between samples

Next we test for differences in microbial load between samples using a two-way ANOVA with the model: *bacterial load \~ line \* condition*.

```{r}
#| label: anova output
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

#bacteria
bDESIGN$microbial_load <- colSums(bCOUNTm_unscaled_ml)
anova <- aov(microbial_load ~ line * condition, data=bDESIGN)
summary(anova) %>% pander(caption="Bacteria: ANOVA")

#fungi
fDESIGN$microbial_load <- colSums(fCOUNTm_unscaled_ml)
anova <- aov(microbial_load ~ line * condition, data=fDESIGN)
summary(anova) %>% pander(caption="Fungi: ANOVA")

#oomycetes
oDESIGN$microbial_load <- colSums(oCOUNTm_unscaled_ml)
anova <- aov(microbial_load ~ line * condition, data=oDESIGN)
summary(anova) %>% pander(caption="Oomycetes: ANOVA")

```

```{r}
#| label: plot microbial load
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 7
#| paged-print: false

library(ggplot2)
library(ggbeeswarm)
library(dplyr)
library(ggpubr)

# General plot function with dynamic y scale
plot_microbial_load <- function(design_df, group_name) {
  y_max <- max(design_df$microbial_load, na.rm = TRUE)
  y_lim <- y_max * 1.6  # Extend the y-axis by 20%

  p <- ggplot(
    design_df,
    aes(x = line, y = microbial_load, fill = condition, alpha = line)
  ) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_point(
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.75),
      size = 1.5,
      color = "black",
      aes(color = condition, shape = line)
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5),
      text = element_text(size = 7),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 7),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 7),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Microbial Load -", group_name),
      x = "Condition",
      y = "Microbial Load",
      fill = "Condition",
      color = "Condition",
      alpha = "Line"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("seagreen", "gold2")) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("seagreen", "gold2")) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(0.9, 0.5)) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, y_lim)) +
    stat_compare_means(
      method = "kruskal.test",
      label = "p",
      label.y = y_lim * 0.95
    )

  return(p)
}


bDESIGN$microbial_load <- colSums(bCOUNTm_unscaled_ml)
fDESIGN$microbial_load <- colSums(fCOUNTm_unscaled_ml)
oDESIGN$microbial_load <- colSums(oCOUNTm_unscaled_ml)

bLOAD_plot <- plot_microbial_load(bDESIGN, "Bacteria")
fLOAD_plot <- plot_microbial_load(fDESIGN, "Fungi")
oLOAD_plot <- plot_microbial_load(oDESIGN, "Oomycetes")

# Combine them

LOAD_plot <- plot_grid(
  bLOAD_plot + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  fLOAD_plot + theme(legend.position = "bottom"),
  oLOAD_plot + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  align = "hv",
  nrow = 1
)

print(LOAD_plot)

ggsave(plot = LOAD_plot, "Output/Figures/microbial_load.pdf", width = 18, height = 8, units = "cm")
```

**Conclusion:** We find differences in microbial loads for WT.

## Export RDS files 2

We export the design-files, normalized, unscaled count-tables with microbial load (without host ASVs), taxonomy-tables and PHYSEQ objects for the following analysis scripts.

```{r}
#| label: export RDA files 2
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

# Export

# create directory
dir.create("interim")
dir.create("interim/02_Taxa_Analysis")

## set output directory
setwd("interim/02_Taxa_Analysis")

#save objects needed in the following scripts

#microbial load samples to be used for beta diversity
saveRDS(bDESIGN, "bDESIGN.RDS")
saveRDS(bCOUNTm_unscaled_ml, "bCOUNTm_microbial_load.RDS")
saveRDS(bTAXA_norm_ml, "bTAXA_microbial_load.RDS")
saveRDS(bPHYSEQ_unscaled_ml, "bPHYSEQ_microbial_load.RDS")

saveRDS(fDESIGN, "fDESIGN.RDS")
saveRDS(fCOUNTm_unscaled_ml, "fCOUNTm_microbial_load.RDS")
saveRDS(fTAXA_norm_ml, "fTAXA_microbial_load.RDS")
saveRDS(fPHYSEQ_unscaled_ml, "fPHYSEQ_microbial_load.RDS")

saveRDS(oDESIGN, "oDESIGN.RDS")
saveRDS(oCOUNTm_unscaled_ml, "oCOUNTm_microbial_load.RDS")
saveRDS(oTAXA_norm_ml, "oTAXA_microbial_load.RDS")
saveRDS(oPHYSEQ_unscaled_ml, "oPHYSEQ_microbial_load.RDS")

```
